title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a typed draft page, numbered '24 bis' and crossed out by hand with large diagonal strokes. It is not about algebraic cycles. It belongs to the theory of Cartan subgroups of smooth group schemes, essentially the material of SGA 3 Exposé XIII ('Sous-groupes de Cartan, éléments réguliers…'), and was evidently filed in cote 14 by accident.

Setting (from 3.1):
- G is a smooth group scheme over S whose Cartan subgroups are representable by a smooth S-scheme 𝒞.
- X ⊂ G_𝒞 is the universal Cartan subgroup, and ψ: X → G_𝒞 → G is the projection.
- U ⊂ G is the open set of regular points. It is defined as the non-vanishing locus G_b of the section b ∈ Γ(G, O_G) from 2.7, a coefficient of the characteristic polynomial of Ad(g) − 1.
- To construct b, S is split as a disjoint sum of pieces S_{n,ρ} on which the relative dimension n and the nilpotent rank ρ are constant. The typescript first wrote 'rang réductif' and corrected it to 'rang nilpotent'.

Proof that ψ^{-1}(U) → U is an isomorphism:
1. Both ψ^{-1}(U) and U are smooth, hence flat and locally of finite presentation over S.
2. So the fibrewise criterion for isomorphism (cited as SGA 1 I 5.7, added by hand) reduces the claim to S = Spec k with k algebraically closed.
3. Over such a k a Cartan subgroup C exists. With N its normalizer, the conjugacy theorem identifies 𝒞 with G/N, and ψ becomes the map G ×^N C → G of no. 2.
4. The statement then follows from 2.6 b): over an algebraically closed field, a regular element lies in exactly one Cartan subgroup.

Maximality of U: U is the largest open V of G with ψ^{-1}(V) → V an isomorphism. The inclusion V ⊂ U can be checked fibre by fibre, where it holds by the field case.

Corollary 3.2: a section g of G that is regular in every fibre lies in a unique Cartan subgroup C of G. Indeed, g is a section of U; a lift of g to X is exactly a pair (C, g ∈ C); and existence and uniqueness of the lift is just a restatement of ψ^{-1}(U) ≅ U.

The page ends by beginning to identify ψ^{-1}(U) with the set of points of X that are regular in their fibre of G_𝒞. The margin note 'indice 𝒞' asks for the subscript 𝒞 to be inserted on G.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The argument tacitly uses that ψ^{-1}(U) is smooth over S (as an open of X, which is smooth over 𝒞, which is smooth over S); the text asserts this without comment. The page itself is crossed out, so it is a superseded draft.
The 'next page' transcription looks like a garbled re-reading of this same text (the variable letters are changed). It should not be relied on.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a discarded typescript draft of SGA 3 Exp. XIII material, which is published. Its only interest is archival: it is misfiled in the cycles dossier, and it records the correction 'rang réductif' → 'rang nilpotent'.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'G_b' is the open set where b is invertible; the NB parenthesis is part of the text.
'sousggroupe' in the typescript is a typo for 'sous-groupe'.
The subscripts on G at the bottom of the page are hand-inserted 𝒞 (G_𝒞), as the margin note 'indice 𝒞' indicates.
The page carries the archive numbering '24 bis', and the whole typed block is crossed out with diagonal pencil lines.
